scope.description: Single-case end-to-end demonstration with unambiguous event identities: a real three-node network with the application caught up, an empty explicit-transition ConfChangeV2 proposed, committed, and applied, recording the log entry type, whether the commit index reached it, and whether the apply panics.
assumptions: Real three-node raft network built with the package test helpers; leader 1 is elected by a MsgHup.

The joint configuration is entered by proposing and committing ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [add node 2, already a voter]} and having every application apply it, so no node outside the network is referenced.

Application progress is simulated by raftLog.appliedTo(committed) on each peer after the joint change commits, the effect of acknowledging applied entries through Advance, which clears the pending-conf guard.

The malformed change is ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, proposed through raft.Step as an EntryConfChangeV2, and the entry is read back from the leader's log at the index it was appended to.
excluded: Any claim about client-side construction of change messages.
Configurations containing nodes absent from the network, which the test helper cannot represent; the earlier attempt that referenced such a node panicked inside the helper rather than in the library.

basis.prefix: TestAssuranceCommittedNonAutoConfChange builds newNetwork(nil, nil, nil), elects leader 1 with a MsgHup, computes the index the joint change will occupy, and proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit, Changes: [AddNode 2]} as an EntryConfChangeV2 through MsgProp. After delivery, every peer's application applies that change and acknowledges applied entries up to its commit index, and a setup event records state, joint flag, voters, outgoing voters, committed, applied, pendingConfIndex and alreadyPending. The test then computes the index the malformed change will occupy, proposes ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} with zero changes, and emits a probe event with that index, the type of the entry read back from the log, the commit index and whether the commit index reached the entry. Finally it applies the malformed change inside a recover and emits whether it panicked, the panic text and whether the configuration is still joint.

comparisons.description: With the guard cleared, the malformed change is accepted and replicated as a configuration-change entry rather than rewritten to a normal entry.
That entry genuinely commits, so it reaches the application in the committed entries it must apply.
Applying the committed configuration-change entry panics, which is the documented action for a committed change the application does not reject.

knowledge.assertion: the pending-conf guard rewrites the entry to EntryNormal unless the application has acknowledged applied entries
with the application caught up the malformed change was kept as EntryConfChangeV2, committed at index 3 and panicked on apply
